span.p:
Static embeddings (Word2Vec / GloVe / FastText)
'bank' gets one vector regardless of context

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 260px; text-align: center; width: 260px;

span.p:
ELMo — contextual embeddings via a bidirectional LSTM
still sequential → can't parallelise, gradients still fade over long sequences

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 260px; text-align: center; width: 260px;

span.p:
Encoder–Decoder (Seq2Seq) — two RNNs, one reads, one writes
everything squeezed through one fixed-size context vector — the bottleneck

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 260px; text-align: center; width: 260px;

span.p:
Attention — the decoder looks back at all encoder states, weighted by relevance
but it only connects two sequences (encoder ↔ decoder); a sentence still can't understand itself

div.style: color: rgb(237, 230, 215) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 260px; text-align: center; width: 260px;

span.p:
Self-attention — the same weighted-lookup idea, a sequence attending to itself
fixes the O(seq length) path between distant tokens → O(1), and the parallelism problem

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 260px; text-align: center; width: 260px;

span.p: Scaled dot-product + multi-head attention — the mechanism, made numerically stable and given several perspectives at once

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 260px; text-align: center; width: 260px;

span.p: Part 3 — assemble the Transformer: + positional encoding, layer norm, residuals, feed-forward, masking → BERT / GPT / T5
